claims.text: US President Donald Trump and top technology executives signed an accord to self-police artificial intelligence during a White House meeting on Tuesday.
Executives attending the White House meeting included OpenAI's Greg Brockman, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Meta's Mark Zuckerberg, Google's Sundar Pichai, and Nvidia's Jensen Huang.
The accord stipulates that companies will implement internal controls, partner with an independent external auditor, and set up a board committee to evaluate audit reports.
Donald Trump described the AI accord to reporters as 'almost like a constitution' and a form of protection.
Donald Trump announced he is considering establishing a 10-person board to monitor AI tool safety and plans to appoint a White House official to lead AI policy.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted from September 17 to 20 found that 73 percent of respondents worry AI companies have not done enough to prevent harm.
OpenAI's Greg Brockman and his wife Anna Brockman donated a combined $25 million to the pro-Trump MAGA Inc PAC in 2025.
Trump administration aides launched a new government service AI tool designed by Airbnb cofounder Joe Gebbia and sponsored by Google, SpaceX, Meta, and 8VC.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order titled 'Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence' directing the federal government to replace the term 'Artificial Intelligence' with 'super intelligence'.
The executive order requires federal agencies to use 'Super Intelligence' and 'SI' in official settings going forward, but does not alter existing regulations or historical records retroactively.
The executive order set a 60-day deadline for the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology to submit proposed legislation to Congress for a statutory definition of super intelligence.
SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk attended the high-level White House luncheon with Donald Trump and other tech CEOs.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton stated that being an AI leader in America is the most important thing for national security.
House Speaker Mike Johnson joined Donald Trump at the White House meeting with tech leaders.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated that AI technology has very real risks and the mechanisms to address them remain under discussion.
Donald Trump promised that the US government would not limit the development of artificial intelligence or support restrictions.

The White House accord outlines four layers of voluntary controls for AI companies covering external auditing, independent board oversight, internal monitoring of security threats, and dedicated internal safety teams.
President Donald Trump ruled out any joint venture with China in artificial intelligence, saying it would be tantamount to giving away secrets.
The US and Beijing launched a new AI dialogue and established a communication channel following Chinese President Xi Jinping's White House visit.
A late September Politico poll showed two out of every three Americans believe there is at least a moderate risk that AI could destroy humanity.
US military forces completed their withdrawal from remaining bases in Iraq on Wednesday.
The withdrawal of US troops from Iraq was agreed upon in 2024 under President Joe Biden and executed under President Donald Trump.
Over 4,500 American service members died in Iraq across more than two decades of war.
Seven of the 18 US service members killed during the 2026 conflict with Iran died in Iraq.
Iraq declared four 'Sovereignty Days' public holidays to mark the complete withdrawal of US military forces.
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi set a target date of June 2027 to disarm all non-state militias in Iraq.
US forces and Iran-aligned militias agreed to refrain from attacks against each other for 90 days following the US departure.
Islamic Resistance in Iraq commander Abu Mojtaba al-Yasiri called the US military departure a historic victory.
Iraqi security officials reported intercepting a suspected Islamic State cell in Kirkuk planning suicide attacks to coincide with the US exit.
The US military completed the exit of its remaining 2,500 troops from Iraq, concluding 12 years of Operation Inherent Resolve.
Three Iranian-made drones targeted a camp affiliated with an Iranian Kurdish opposition group in Erbil on Monday.
US Army soldiers fully withdrew from the US military base located in Baghdad.
UK counter-terrorism police investigated five men arrested near RAF Fairford after finding petrol but no explosives inside three vans.
One of the five arrested suspects called 999 to report the incident before armed officers arrived.
UK Counter Terrorism Policing chief Laurence Taylor confirmed that extensive examinations found no improvised explosive devices in the seized vans.
UK official Andy Burnham called a meeting of the Cobra crisis committee on Monday due to concerns over potential state-sponsored proxy involvement.
Eighty-five households in the village of Whelford were evacuated during the security alert near RAF Fairford.
Police investigators confirmed the five arrested men were not fuel thieves, despite the vans bearing fake delivery logos.
US President Donald Trump publicly criticized the UK decision to grant bail to the five suspects in the RAF Fairford probe.
A local farmer alerted police after seeing three vans blocking a road and masked men fleeing the site near RAF Fairford.
In March, the UK government granted permission to the US military to use RAF Fairford for specific defensive strikes against Iran.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated the incident near RAF Fairford was a very serious situation involving the hand of a foreign actor.
UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting emphasized that granting bail to suspects is an operational matter for police, not politicians.
The US Supreme Court granted an emergency request allowing the Trump administration to resume third-country deportations.
The Supreme Court agreed to hear formal oral arguments on the legality of third-country deportations in December.
Federal attorneys stated a lower court injunction had forced the cancellation of a deportation flight carrying about 70 people to three countries.
Human rights groups estimate over 25,000 people have been deported to 29 third countries under the Trump administration's policy.
A US Senate resolution requiring a report on West Bank violence failed in a 47 to 51 vote.
Supreme Court Justices Sonia Sotomayor, Ketanji Brown Jackson, and Elena Kagan dissented from granting the stay to resume deportations.
US Solicitor General John Sauer argued that rapid third-country deportation is an essential tool to remove criminal aliens.
At least 35 countries have signed agreements with the US to accept third-country deportees.
Burundi signed an agreement with the US to accept non-citizen deportees who do not face prosecution and lack terrorism links.
United Nations human rights experts sent a letter to the US government urging an immediate halt to third-country removals.
